title: M19. Compositional security against super-rushing
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Can super-rushing protocols — where parties may act on predictions of others' future messages — be given a security notion that survives composition? The goal is a useful composable security definition and a composition theorem for such protocols, together with sufficient causal and state-isolation conditions under which secure subprotocols remain secure when combined.
status: The 2025 work (Asharov–Chandramouli–Cohen–Ishai, *Peeking Into the Future*, 2025) shows that even sequential composition can fail to preserve super-rushing security.
solved_when: A composable security definition for super-rushing protocols is formulated, a composition theorem is proven for it, and sufficient causal and state-isolation conditions are identified.
why: Individually secure subprotocols must remain secure when assembled into larger workflows; without such a theorem, super-rushing security cannot be safely used in any modular protocol design.
key_works: Asharov–Chandramouli–Cohen–Ishai (2025), [*Peeking Into the Future*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1394); Canetti (2001), [*Universally Composable Security: A New Paradigm for Cryptographic Protocols*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2000/067).

title: M21. Complete fairness classification for asymmetric Boolean functionalities
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Which two-party Boolean functionalities that give the parties different outputs can be computed with complete fairness? The goal is a full classification: an effectively checkable criterion for fairness, with matching protocol constructions for the feasible cases and impossibility proofs for the rest.
status: Symmetric Boolean functionalities were fully classified by Asharov–Beimel–Makriyannis–Omri (2015) in [*Complete Characterization of Fairness in Secure Two-Party Computation of Boolean Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/1000). The 2017 construction framework of Daza–Makriyannis, [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098), addressed the asymmetric setting but unresolved cases remain.
solved_when: A complete, effectively checkable characterization of asymmetric Boolean two-party functionalities exists, together with constructions for every functionality the criterion admits fairness for and impossibility results for every functionality it excludes, leaving no unresolved cases.
why: It determines exactly when complete fairness is achievable without an honest majority or a trusted third party, settling the limits of fair secure two-party computation for Boolean functions.
key_works: Asharov–Beimel–Makriyannis–Omri (2015), [*Complete Characterization of Fairness in Secure Two-Party Computation of Boolean Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/1000); Daza–Makriyannis (2017), [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098).

title: M22. Fairness classification beyond Boolean outputs
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Which two-party functionalities with arbitrary finite output domains admit complete fairness, in both deterministic and randomized settings? Formally, give necessary and sufficient conditions for completely fair computation of arbitrary finite-output two-party functionalities.
status: Boolean classifications, constant-domain constructions, and reductions to fair coin tossing provide partial structure, without a universal classification. Key works include Daza–Makriyannis (2017), [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098), and Asharov–Lindell–Rabin (2013), [*Full Characterization of Functions that Imply Fair Coin Tossing and Ramifications to Fairness*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/110).
solved_when: A characterization is available that, for any deterministic or randomized two-party functionality with finite output domains, determines whether complete fairness is achievable — closing the gap left by Boolean and constant-domain partial results.
why: Auctions, exchanges, and private analytics produce richer outputs than a shared bit, so fairness results restricted to Boolean or constant domains do not cover the functionalities that actually arise in practice.
key_works: Daza–Makriyannis (2017), [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098); Asharov–Lindell–Rabin (2013), [*Full Characterization of Functions that Imply Fair Coin Tossing and Ramifications to Fairness*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/110).

title: M23. Fairness with a growing dishonest majority
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Which families of symmetric Boolean functions can still be computed fairly when the number of parties is polynomial in the security parameter and dishonest parties outnumber honest ones by a margin that grows with \(n\)? More precisely, characterize the efficiently realizable fair symmetric Boolean function families when \(n=\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) and corruption exceeds \(n/2\) by a growing amount.
status: Dachman-Soled (2020), [*Revisiting Fairness in MPC: Polynomial Number of Parties and General Adversarial Structures*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1430), obtains broad families of fairly computable functions at \(n/2\) corruption and majority at \(n/2+c\) for fixed constants \(c\); the case of a growing surplus remains distinct and open.
solved_when: A characterization is given of the symmetric Boolean function families admitting efficient fair MPC protocols for \(n=\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) parties tolerating corruption exceeding \(n/2\) by a growing surplus — showing which families are realizable and which are not.
why: It would identify which collective decisions remain fair despite substantial collusion, and where fairness provably breaks down as the dishonest majority grows.
key_works: Dachman-Soled (2020), [*Revisiting Fairness in MPC: Polynomial Number of Parties and General Adversarial Structures*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1430).

title: M24. Exact cryptographic strength of a small trusted intervention
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: How much trust must a minimal "trusted helper" provide for fully secure multiparty computation on arbitrary circuits — specifically, when that helper is consulted only once and performs work independent of the circuit being computed? A complete answer would characterize exactly which cryptographic assumptions are necessary and sufficient for such a general, fully secure MPC protocol.
status: The 2022 minimal-trust work of Ishai–Patra–Patranabis–Ravi–Srinivasan ([*Fully-Secure MPC with Minimal Trust*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1248)) gives succinct-FE constructions and lower bounds for restricted approaches; the unrestricted characterization remains open.
solved_when: A characterization is given of the assumptions that are both necessary and sufficient for fully secure MPC for general functionalities, using a trusted party invoked exactly once whose computation is independent of the circuit size; no restriction is placed on the protocol class.
why: It settles how much cryptographic machinery is genuinely required to shrink trusted computation to a single, circuit-independent intervention, and identifies the boundary between achievable and impossible minimal-trust designs.
key_works: Ishai–Patra–Patranabis–Ravi–Srinivasan (2022), [*Fully-Secure MPC with Minimal Trust*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1248).

title: M28. Three-round plain-model ZK from polynomial hardness
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can three-message zero-knowledge arguments with negligible soundness error for all of NP be constructed in the plain model from standard polynomial-time hardness assumptions alone? In particular, can the extra keyless multi-collision-resistant-hash assumption required by current constructions be eliminated?
status: Three-round zero knowledge in this setting is established: Kiyoshima's 2026 journal result constructs public-coin three-round ZK from LWE plus keyless multi-collision resistance secure against slightly superpolynomial adversaries. Removing the nonstandard hashing hypothesis while keeping only polynomial hardness remains open.
solved_when: A three-round, negligible-soundness-error zero-knowledge argument for NP in the plain model exists, proved secure under conventional polynomial hardness assumptions, with no keyless multi-collision-resistance hypothesis (or other superpolynomial-hardness assumption).
why: It would pinpoint exactly which assumptions suffice to cross the classical black-box simulation barriers for three-round zero knowledge, separating what is achievable from what the barriers actually forbid.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2026), [*Public-Coin Three-Round Zero-Knowledge from Learning with Errors and Keyless Multi-Collision-Resistant Hash*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-025-09551-8).

title: M29. Complexity-only lower bounds for three-round ZK proofs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can we rule out three-round negligible-error zero-knowledge proofs for NP using only ordinary complexity separations, even when non-black-box simulation is allowed?
status: The 2018 impossibility of Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain, [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167), rules out such proofs but only under program-obfuscation assumptions; three-round computationally sound arguments do not settle the proof question.
solved_when: A proof (under standard complexity assumptions such as NP ≠ BPP) that no three-round negligible-error zero-knowledge proof system for NP exists, permitting non-black-box simulators and relying on no cryptographic assumptions like program obfuscation.
why: It would show the three-round barrier is an intrinsic limit of interaction rather than an artifact of powerful cryptographic assumptions.
key_works: Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain (2018), [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167).

title: M30. Four-round ZK proofs with non-black-box simulation
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Does every language in NP have a zero-knowledge proof that uses only four messages, has negligible soundness error, and can be simulated by inspecting the verifier's code rather than treating it as a black box? Or is there a matching lower bound showing that four rounds are unattainable under conventional assumptions?
status: Five-round proofs are known, while four-round black-box proofs face lower bounds; existing three-round impossibilities leave this four-round boundary distinct. Key references include Katz (2008), [*Which Languages Have 4-Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs?*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-78524-8_5), and Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain (2018), [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167).
solved_when: Either a four-message negligible-error zero-knowledge proof for NP with non-black-box (code-aware) simulation is constructed from a standard assumption, or a lower bound is proved ruling out such proofs under conventional assumptions.
why: It tests whether inspecting the verifier's code can save a round of interaction while unconditional soundness is retained, pinpointing whether the known round barrier is an artifact of black-box simulation.
key_works: Katz (2008), [*Which Languages Have 4-Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs?*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-78524-8_5); Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain (2018), [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167).

title: M32. Constant-round concurrent ZK from ordinary OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct constant-round concurrent ZK for NP from arbitrary polynomially secure OWFs in the plain model, with ordinary polynomial-time simulation.
status: OWF-based concurrent protocols and stronger-assumption constant-round protocols exist; the combined target remains open.
why: Would provide low-latency concurrent privacy from the basic symmetric-cryptography assumption.
key_works: Chung–Lin–Pass (2015), [*Constant-Round Concurrent Zero-Knowledge from Indistinguishability Obfuscation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/991); Pass (2021), [*A Tutorial on Concurrent Zero Knowledge*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/615).

title: M34. Four-round statistical nonmalleable ZK from weaker assumptions
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can we build a four-round statistical nonmalleable zero-knowledge protocol for NP assuming only arbitrary one-way functions? More precisely, the goal is a construction achieving negligible soundness and zero-knowledge errors together with delayed-input one-many simulation extractability, from OWFs alone.
status: Kiyoshima’s 2025 result, revised in 2026, achieves the target security properties from collision-resistant hashes and injective one-way functions.
solved_when: A four-round statistical nonmalleable zero-knowledge argument for NP is constructed from arbitrary one-way functions, preserving negligible errors and delayed-input one-many simulation extractability.
why: It would combine statistical privacy, low interaction, and minimal assumptions in a single primitive — removing the need for structured assumptions like collision-resistant or injective one-way functions.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2025/2026), [*Four-round Statistical Non-malleable Zero-knowledge*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1787); Kiyoshima (2020), [*Statistical Concurrent Non-Malleable Zero-Knowledge from One-Way Functions*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-020-09348-x).

title: M37. Constant-round simultaneous resettability from OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can we build a constant-round zero-knowledge protocol for NP that is resettably sound and resettably zero-knowledge, assuming only polynomially secure one-way functions? Equivalently, the goal is simultaneous resettability — privacy preserved under prover resets and soundness preserved under verifier resets — in a constant number of rounds from this minimal assumption.
status: Simultaneous resettability from one-way functions is known with polynomially many rounds (Chung–Ostrovsky–Pass–Visconti, [Simultaneous Resettability from One-Way Functions](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~rafael/papers/focs13srzk.pdf), 2013); constant-round constructions exist but rely on stronger tools (Chongchitmate–Ostrovsky–Visconti, [Resettably-Sound Resettable Zero Knowledge in Constant Rounds](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-70503-3_4), 2017).
solved_when: A constant-round resettably-sound resettable zero-knowledge protocol for NP is constructed from polynomially secure one-way functions alone.
why: It would protect resettable devices (smart cards, sealed tokens) without requiring obfuscation-scale assumptions or stronger tools, closing the gap between feasibility and round efficiency.
key_works: Chung–Ostrovsky–Pass–Visconti (2013), [*Simultaneous Resettability from One-Way Functions*](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~rafael/papers/focs13srzk.pdf); Chongchitmate–Ostrovsky–Visconti (2017), [*Resettably-Sound Resettable Zero Knowledge in Constant Rounds*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-70503-3_4).

title: M38. Low-overhead resettable statistical ZK
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can resettable statistical zero-knowledge arguments for NP be implemented with only near-linear overhead in the prover's work, starting from a specified witness-encryption instantiation? A satisfactory answer should make explicit how the overhead scales with the witness length, the number of resets, and the security loss.
status: The state of the art is qualitative: the 2024 equivalence between resettable statistical ZK arguments and witness encryption, assuming OWFs (Kiyoshimа 2024, *Resettable Statistical Zero-Knowledge for NP*, https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/806), with no efficient instantiation worked out.
solved_when: A construction of resettable statistical ZK from a concrete witness-encryption scheme whose prover overhead is near-linear, with an analysis accounting for witness length, reset count, and security loss.
why: It would separate the unavoidable strength of the underlying assumptions from the avoidable cost of the implementation, making the 2024 equivalence practical.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2024), [*Resettable Statistical Zero-Knowledge for NP*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/806).

title: M41. NIZK from arbitrary public-key encryption
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can every semantically secure public-key encryption scheme yield noninteractive zero-knowledge arguments for NP in the CRS model? Formally, construct reusable CRS-model NIZK arguments for NP from arbitrary semantically secure PKE, without assuming additional encryption structure or correlation-intractable hashing.
status: The problem is long-standing. Recent constructions — e.g., Branco et al. (2025), *Black-Box Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge from Vector Trapdoor Hash*, and Dao–Jain–Jin (2024), *Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge from LPN and MQ* — broaden the concrete assumption families supporting NIZK, but no generic reduction from CPA-secure PKE is known.
solved_when: A construction is given (with a proof of soundness and zero knowledge) that treats any CPA-secure PKE scheme as a black-box-style generic primitive, adding no structural assumptions on the encryption scheme or auxiliary primitives such as correlation-intractable hashing.
why: It would establish that noninteractive privacy for NP requires no additional primitive beyond generic public-key confidentiality, pinning down the minimal assumption behind NIZK.
key_works: Branco et al. (2025), [*Black-Box Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge from Vector Trapdoor Hash*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1514); Dao–Jain–Jin (2024), [*Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge from LPN and MQ*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1254).

title: M42. Fully black-box reusable NIZK from vector trapdoor hashing
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can the vector-trapdoor-hash approach to NIZKs be extended from a single proof to an adaptively secure, multi-theorem zero-knowledge system while remaining fully black-box in its underlying primitives? Formally, this asks for a black-box construction achieving adaptive multi-theorem zero knowledge from vector trapdoor hashing.
status: The 2025 construction of Branco–Choudhuri–Döttling–Jain–Malavolta–Srinivasan (2025/2026) gives single-theorem black-box NIZK from vector trapdoor hashing ([*Black-Box Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge from Vector Trapdoor Hash*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1514)); its multi-theorem upgrade explicitly uses cryptography non-black-box.
solved_when: A NIZK construction based on vector trapdoor hashing achieves adaptive multi-theorem zero knowledge with proofs for many statements under one setup, and is fully black-box in its use of the cryptographic primitives.
why: It would preserve the modularity of black-box constructions while allowing a single setup to support many proofs, removing the current need to invoke cryptography non-black-box.
key_works: Branco–Choudhuri–Döttling–Jain–Malavolta–Srinivasan (2025/2026), [*Black-Box Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge from Vector Trapdoor Hash*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1514).

title: M43. Efficient-prover ZAPs from OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct two-message public-coin witness-indistinguishable proofs for NP from OWFs with a prover polynomial in instance and witness length.
status: Ball–Dachman-Soled obtain OWF-based ZAPs with prover time \(2^{n^\varepsilon}\) for every fixed positive \(\varepsilon\).
why: Would make minimal-assumption two-message proofs computationally usable.
key_works: Ball–Dachman-Soled (2023/2025), [*(Inefficient Prover) ZAPs from Hard-to-Invert Functions*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/205/).

title: M44. Statistical ZAPs from polynomially hard LWE
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can two-message public-coin statistically witness-indistinguishable arguments (statistical ZAPs) be built from polynomially hard LWE? The construction should achieve polynomial modulus-to-noise ratio and negligible soundness error.
status: The 2025 hidden-bits construction (Bradley–Lu–Nassar–Waters–Wu, [*A Hidden-Bits Approach to Statistical ZAPs from LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1663)) obtains nonadaptive soundness but relies on quasi-polynomial hardness of LWE.
solved_when: A statistical ZAP from LWE with polynomial hardness (not quasi-polynomial), polynomial modulus-to-noise ratio, negligible soundness error, and two public-coin messages exists.
why: It would eliminate the significant quantitative hardness penalty currently attached to compact statistical privacy, removing the need for complexity leveraging.
key_works: Bradley–Lu–Nassar–Waters–Wu (2025), [*A Hidden-Bits Approach to Statistical ZAPs from LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1663).

title: M45. Adaptively sound statistical ZAPs without length-specific leverage
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can statistical ZAPs with adaptive soundness be built for statements of arbitrary polynomial length, assuming only polynomial or quasi-polynomial LWE hardness, with no setup parameters fixed in advance to a bound on future statement lengths?
status: The 2025 construction of Bradley–Lu–Nassar–Waters–Wu ([*A Hidden-Bits Approach to Statistical ZAPs from LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1663)) obtains adaptive soundness under subexponential LWE hardness, but only for an a priori bounded statement length.
solved_when: A construction exists achieving adaptive soundness for unrestricted polynomial statement lengths from polynomial or quasi-polynomial LWE hardness, with no setup tied to the largest statement length.
why: Long-lived public parameters issued once should remain usable for statements chosen later, rather than being invalidated or needing reissue once longer statements appear.
key_works: Bradley–Lu–Nassar–Waters–Wu (2025), [*A Hidden-Bits Approach to Statistical ZAPs from LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1663).

title: M46. LPN-and-MQ NIZK without exponential MQ hardness
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can we build a non-interactive zero-knowledge proof system for NP from only polynomially hard assumptions — ordinary LPN and random underdetermined multivariate quadratic equations — without requiring exponential hardness of MQ? The construction should state explicitly whether zero-knowledge privacy is computational or statistical.
status: Dao–Jain–Jin (2024), in [*Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge from LPN and MQ*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1254), construct NIZK using polynomially hard LPN combined with exponentially hard MQ for computational zero knowledge; their statistical zero-knowledge variant additionally relies on dense-sparse LPN.
solved_when: A NIZK for NP is constructed assuming only polynomial hardness of standard LPN and random underdetermined MQ, with the privacy guarantee (computational vs. statistical) explicitly specified.
why: It would weaken the assumptions underpinning a non-LWE route to NIZK, replacing the exponential MQ hardness currently needed with polynomial hardness.
key_works: Dao–Jain–Jin (2024), [*Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge from LPN and MQ*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1254).

title: M47. Statistical-privacy-preserving NIZK amplification
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can a nontrivial weak statistical NIZK be amplified to negligible soundness and privacy errors while keeping statistical privacy intact, relying only on OWFs for proofs and PKE for arguments, with no additional collision-resistant hashing?
status: Ordinary amplification is established under those respective assumptions; known preservation of statistical ZK and succinctness uses CRH, per Applebaum–Kachlon (2025), [*NIZK Amplification via Leakage-Resilient Secure Computation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/995).
solved_when: An amplification procedure exists for weak statistical NIZKs achieving negligible error under OWFs (for proofs) and PKE (for arguments), preserving statistical privacy and succinctness without additional CRH.
why: It would preserve the strongest privacy guarantees while repairing weak security parameters, avoiding the extra CRH assumption currently needed.
key_works: Applebaum–Kachlon (2025), [*NIZK Amplification via Leakage-Resilient Secure Computation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/995).

title: M49. Near-linear secret sharing of NP statements
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Can an NP statement be secret-shared among n parties so that each party's share and the total computation scale near-linearly in the instance and witness sizes? Formally, the goal is threshold NP-statement secret sharing with total transformed-instance size and computation \(\widetilde O(n(|x|+|w|)\operatorname{poly}(\lambda))\), while retaining the full threshold range and the required privacy.
status: All-threshold polynomial feasibility was established in 2025 by Applebaum–Kachlon, [*How to Share an NP Statement or Combiners for Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/334); the near-linear target remains a stricter proposed refinement.
solved_when: A construction achieves total transformed-instance size and computation \(\widetilde O(n(|x|+|w|)\operatorname{poly}(\lambda))\) for the full threshold range with the required privacy.
why: It would sharply reduce the cost of distributing logical evidence and of combining proof systems across parties.
key_works: Applebaum–Kachlon (2025), [*How to Share an NP Statement or Combiners for Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/334).

title: A02. General iO from one conventional pairing assumption
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Can general-purpose indistinguishability obfuscation be based on a single conventional pairing assumption such as SXDH or DLIN? More precisely, is there a construction of iO whose security rests on one standard bilinear-map assumption alone, with no independent noisy-learning or coding-theoretic assumption?
status: The current frontier is Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan's 2024 construction, which achieves iO from DLIN together with large-field and sparse-binary LPN variants, while removing a previously separate local-PRG assumption.
solved_when: A construction of general iO is given whose sole assumption is a conventional pairing assumption (e.g., SXDH or DLIN), eliminating the additional large-field and sparse-binary LPN components and any other independent noisy-learning or coding assumptions.
why: It would simplify the logical foundation of obfuscation and reduce the cryptanalytic surface to a single well-studied assumption, making security evaluations far more tractable.
key_works: Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [*Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).

title: A05. General iO from iPRO without extra algebraic assumptions
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Can indistinguishability obfuscation for general circuits be derived from obfuscation for identical pseudorandom functions (iPRO) in the standard model, without adding pairing assumptions?
status: The 2025 PRO work (Branco–Döttling–Jain–Malavolta–Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan, 2024/2025, [*Pseudorandom Obfuscation and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1742)) derives iO from iPRO plus pairings, and stronger results from iPRO in a pseudorandom-oracle model.
solved_when: A proof (or construction) establishes general iO from iPRO alone in the standard model, with no extra algebraic assumptions such as pairings.
why: It would clarify the exact power of a restricted obfuscation notion, showing whether iPRO alone already suffices for full iO.
key_works: Branco–Döttling–Jain–Malavolta–Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024/2025), [*Pseudorandom Obfuscation and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1742).

title: A09. Exact source conditions for compute-and-compare obfuscation
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: What is the exact threshold of unpredictability a hidden comparison target must satisfy for compute-and-compare obfuscation to be possible from polynomially secure LWE — including how auxiliary information about the target may degrade it? A complete answer would give matching positive and negative results pinning down the weakest sufficient conditions.
status: The 2017 construction of Wichs–Zirdelis ([*Obfuscating Compute-and-Compare Programs under LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/276)) covers broad sufficient-pseudoentropy regimes; the matching positive and negative boundaries of the assumption landscape remain incomplete.
solved_when: A characterization of the weakest target-unpredictability and auxiliary-information conditions under which compute-and-compare obfuscation follows from polynomially secure LWE is established, with matching lower bounds showing the conditions cannot be weakened.
why: Applications vary sharply in how predictable their hidden comparison targets are, so tight conditions determine exactly which real-world programs can be obfuscated and which provably cannot.
key_works: Wichs–Zirdelis (2017), [*Obfuscating Compute-and-Compare Programs under LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/276).

title: A11. A 100-fold-overhead iO demonstrator
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Can general-purpose indistinguishability obfuscation be made concretely usable — an actual, runnable demonstrator rather than an asymptotic construction? Formally, produce proof-backed general iO where both obfuscated-code size and evaluation time are within \(100\times\) of the unobfuscated baseline at a stated 128-bit classical security target, evaluated on a public circuit suite.
status: A proposed moonshot. Current work establishes feasibility and quasi-linear asymptotics — via Jain–Lin–Sahai (2020/2021), [*Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09317), and Ma–Dai–Shi (2025), [*Quasi-Linear Indistinguishability Obfuscation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/307) — but these do not establish the concrete \(100\times\) envelope targeted here.
solved_when: A proof-backed general iO scheme is implemented and demonstrated on a public circuit suite, with measured code size and evaluation time each at most \(100\times\) the baseline, at a stated 128-bit classical security target.
why: It would turn general obfuscation from a theoretical capability into an experimentally assessable technology, with measurable costs that practitioners and cryptanalysts can evaluate.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2020/2021), [*Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09317); Ma–Dai–Shi (2025), [*Quasi-Linear Indistinguishability Obfuscation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/307).

title: A13. Fully collusion-resistant circuit FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can we build a public-key functional encryption scheme for arbitrary circuits, secure against any polynomial number of colluding key holders, under only the standard Learning with Errors assumption? Formally, the target is an LWE-based scheme whose ciphertext size is independent of both the number of key queries and the size of the supported circuits.
status: General compact FE is currently known only from stronger obfuscation-related assumptions (Garg et al. 2013/2016, Candidate Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption for all Circuits), while bounded-collusion FE from minimal assumptions, e.g. Ananth–Vaikuntanathan 2019, Optimal Bounded-Collusion Secure Functional Encryption, incurs ciphertexts that grow with the collusion bound.
solved_when: A publicly key-generation-based FE scheme for arbitrary circuits is constructed and proven secure from ordinary LWE, tolerating any polynomial number of key queries, with ciphertext size bounded independently of both the collusion count and the supported circuit size.
why: It would give general controlled disclosure of computed functions over encrypted data from a conventional, well-studied lattice assumption, removing the need for exotic tools like obfuscation.
key_works: Garg et al. (2013/2016), [*Candidate Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption for all Circuits*](https://doi.org/10.1137/14095772X); Ananth–Vaikuntanathan (2019), [*Optimal Bounded-Collusion Secure Functional Encryption*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/314).

title: A16. Unleveled ABE from ordinary circular LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can fully collusion-resistant attribute-based encryption for unbounded-depth circuits be built from ordinary LWE together with a conventional circular-security assumption? Formally, the goal is such an ABE scheme whose security reduces to standard LWE plus ordinary circular security, without any evasive-circular assumption.
status: Ordinary circular security is currently known to yield unbounded-depth single-key FE, single-key ABE, and reusable garbling; achieving full ABE and predicate encryption has so far required evasive-circular LWE, as in Hsieh–Lin–Luo (2023/2025), [*Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices: Garbled Circuits of Optimal Size, Laconic Functional Evaluation, and More*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716).
solved_when: A fully collusion-resistant ABE scheme supporting unbounded-depth circuits is constructed and proven secure under ordinary LWE plus conventional circular security alone.
why: It would remove the predetermined depth ceiling on supported circuits without escalating to a specialized assumption like evasive-circular LWE.
key_works: Hsieh–Lin–Luo (2023/2025), [*Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices: Garbled Circuits of Optimal Size, Laconic Functional Evaluation, and More*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716).

title: A17. Simultaneously optimal circuit-ABE components
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can a circuit attribute-based encryption scheme under ordinary LWE have public parameters, ciphertexts, and secret keys whose cryptographic sizes are all simultaneously independent of the policy size and depth, with policy descriptions supplied externally rather than embedded?
status: Polynomial-in-security-parameter secret keys are known (Cini–Wee 2023/2025, [ABE for Circuits with poly(λ)-Sized Keys from LWE](https://doi.org/10.1137/24M1636162)), and ABE for circuits of unbounded depth from lattices is known (Hsieh–Lin–Luo 2023/2025, [Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716)); however, small keys alone do not achieve the full simultaneous compactness target.
solved_when: A circuit ABE scheme from standard LWE exists in which the cryptographic portions of public parameters, ciphertexts, and secret keys are all simultaneously independent of policy size and depth, and public descriptions are allowed externally.
why: Optimizing one component can merely shift the cost into another, so only simultaneous compactness delivers genuinely succinct circuit ABE.
key_works: Cini–Wee (2023/2025), [*ABE for Circuits with poly(\(\lambda\))-Sized Keys from LWE*](https://doi.org/10.1137/24M1636162); Hsieh–Lin–Luo (2023/2025), [*Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716).

title: A18. Fully attribute-hiding predicate encryption for circuits
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can we build predicate encryption for arbitrary circuits from LWE that is fully attribute-hiding — that is, even a key holder authorized to decrypt learns nothing about the encrypted attribute beyond what their own decryption outcome reveals? Formally, the scheme should hide the challenge attribute pair (x₀, x₁) whenever f(x₀) = f(x₁) for the queried key's predicate f.
status: Circuit predicate encryption from LWE with weak attribute hiding is established, due to Gorbunov–Vaikuntanathan–Wee (2015), [*Predicate Encryption for Circuits from LWE*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-48000-7_25); however, its security proof restricts the adversary to keys that reject both challenge attributes, which does not meet the stronger fully attribute-hiding target.
solved_when: An LWE-based predicate encryption scheme for circuits exists whose security proof establishes attribute hiding even against keys authorized on both challenge attributes (i.e., whenever the authorized outputs agree), rather than only against keys that reject both.
why: In applications such as privacy-preserving classification, a user's key should let them learn the authorized outcome without leaking unrelated properties of the encrypted data; weak attribute hiding permits exactly this kind of auxiliary-information leakage.
key_works: Gorbunov–Vaikuntanathan–Wee (2015), [*Predicate Encryption for Circuits from LWE*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-48000-7_25).

title: A19. General registered FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can we build fully collusion-resistant registered functional encryption for general circuits from the plain Learning with Errors assumption, where users generate their own keys independently and a succinct aggregated key is produced by an untrusted curator?
status: Known general constructions rely on powerful primitives rather than plain LWE; recent lattice-based results cover pseudorandom functionalities (Pal–Schädlich–Tairi, 2025, [Registered Functional Encryption for Pseudorandom Functionalities from Lattices](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/967)) or bounded-collusion settings under additional assumptions (Zhang–Chen–He–Zhang, 2024/2025, [Bounded Collusion-Resistant Registered Functional Encryption for Circuits](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1572)).
solved_when: A construction of registered FE for circuits from ordinary LWE exists that achieves full collusion resistance, independent key generation, and succinct aggregation by an untrusted curator, with a security proof from standard LWE.
why: It would eliminate the central secret-key generation step from general functional encryption, removing the trusted key-issuing authority that currently sits at the heart of such systems.
key_works: Pal–Schädlich–Tairi (2025), [*Registered Functional Encryption for Pseudorandom Functionalities from Lattices*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/967); Zhang–Chen–He–Zhang (2024/2025), [*Bounded Collusion-Resistant Registered Functional Encryption for Circuits*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1572).

title: A21. Depth-independent registered ABE from succinct LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can registered attribute-based encryption for circuits be built from succinct LWE so that parameters do not degrade with circuit depth, while still supporting unboundedly many (polynomially many) users and succinct parameters?
status: Wee–Wu (2025) achieve components of size poly(λ, d, log N); known depth-independent alternatives rely on stronger machinery.
solved_when: A registered circuit ABE scheme from succinct LWE whose component sizes are independent of the circuit depth d, retain succinct parameters, and support unboundedly many users.
why: It would free practitioners from sizing keys and ciphertexts around the deepest policy that might ever be used.
key_works: Wee–Wu (2025), [*Unbounded Distributed Broadcast Encryption and Registered ABE from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1039).

title: A23. Remove random oracles from succinct registered circuit ABE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can the nearly optimal parameter envelope achieved for succinct registered circuit ABE from succinct LWE be realized in the plain model, without random oracles, while still supporting unbounded polynomially many independent user keys? In other words, is the random oracle in the current constructions merely an artifact, or is some idealized assumption essential to that parameter regime?
status: The relevant 2025 constructions — Wee–Wu (2025), *Unbounded Distributed Broadcast Encryption and Registered ABE from Succinct LWE*, and Champion–Hsieh–Wu (2025), *Registered ABE and Adaptively-Secure Broadcast Encryption from Succinct LWE* — use random oracles; removing depth dependence is a separate problem.
solved_when: A registered-circuit-ABE scheme in the standard (plain) model, based on succinct LWE, achieves the nearly optimal parameter envelope of the random-oracle constructions and supports unbounded polynomially many independent user keys.
why: It would replace the idealized hashing of the random-oracle model with a concrete standard-model foundation, making the security of succinct registered ABE unconditional on heuristic instantiation assumptions.
key_works: Wee–Wu (2025), [*Unbounded Distributed Broadcast Encryption and Registered ABE from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1039); Champion–Hsieh–Wu (2025), [*Registered ABE and Adaptively-Secure Broadcast Encryption from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/044).

title: A25. Malicious-client-secure circuit multi-client ABE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can multi-client attribute-based encryption for general circuits be made secure when a substantial fraction of clients act maliciously, while still allowing clients to encrypt independently and ensuring that combined ciphertexts are bound to their intended identifiers?
status: The 2025 introduction by Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), [*Lattice-based Multi-Authority/Client Attribute-based Encryption for Circuits*](https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/1), provides circuit constructions with limited adaptivity and corrupted-client security.
solved_when: An adaptive multi-client circuit ABE scheme exists that tolerates substantial malicious-client participation, supports independent encryption by each client, and securely binds ciphertext combinations to identifiers.
why: Without it, independently supplied encrypted inputs open the door to cross-session and substitution attacks, undermining the integrity of any aggregation relying on them.
key_works: Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), [*Lattice-based Multi-Authority/Client Attribute-based Encryption for Circuits*](https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/1).

title: A27. General multi-input FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Can we build compact multi-input functional encryption for arbitrary circuits — supporting repeated ciphertexts and security for all authorized cross-combinations — under only the ordinary Learning with Errors assumption?
status: General multi-input functional encryption is currently known only from powerful obfuscation assumptions; results under weaker assumptions restrict the functionality or the security notion. See Goldwasser et al. (2014), [Multi-input Functional Encryption](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-55220-5_32).
solved_when: A construction of compact multi-input FE for arbitrary circuits from ordinary LWE is given, handling repeated ciphertexts and proven secure for all authorized cross-combinations of inputs.
why: It would allow controlled computation over independently encrypted data from multiple sources without relying on heavy obfuscation assumptions, unlocking distributed query privacy and limiting leakage from Cartesian products.
key_works: Goldwasser et al. (2014), [*Multi-input Functional Encryption*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-55220-5_32).

title: A30. Witness encryption for NP from ordinary LWE
subfield: Witness encryption and condition-based cryptography
open: Can we build witness encryption for all of NP assuming only the standard Learning With Errors (LWE) assumption? That is, a polynomial-time construction of witness encryption for NP from ordinary LWE, without relying on stronger evasive-LWE hypotheses.
status: Open since witness encryption's introduction in 2013. Direct lattice-based candidates rely on evasive assumptions, such as Tsabary (2022), [*Candidate Witness Encryption from Lattice Techniques*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-15802-5_19) and Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs (2022), [*Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140); recent generic-group results address a different model.
solved_when: A polynomial-time witness encryption scheme for all of NP is constructed and proved secure under the ordinary LWE assumption alone, with no evasive-LWE or related nonstandard hypotheses.
why: It would deliver encrypt-to-condition functionality — encrypting to any NP statement so only holders of a witness can decrypt — under a central post-quantum assumption, making the primitive far more trustworthy and broadly usable.
key_works: Tsabary (2022), [*Candidate Witness Encryption from Lattice Techniques*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-15802-5_19); Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs (2022), [*Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140).

title: A34. Succinct WE from ordinary iO
subfield: Witness encryption and condition-based cryptography
open: Can succinct witness encryption be built from ordinary indistinguishability obfuscation plus standard auxiliary assumptions? Formally, the goal is a ciphertext of length poly(λ, |x|, log |C|, log m) for a verification circuit C and witness bound m, with public descriptions kept external.
status: Ordinary (non-succinct) witness encryption follows from iO; the stronger succinctness target currently requires stronger obfuscation or extraction notions.
solved_when: A witness encryption scheme derived from ordinary iO (with standard auxiliaries) achieves ciphertext length poly(λ, |x|, log |C|, log m) for verification circuit C and witness bound m, with public descriptions external.
why: It would separate ciphertext cost from witness and verification complexity, making encryption cheap even for complex statements.
key_works: Devadas–Jain–Waters–Wu (2025), [*Succinct Witness Encryption for Batch Languages and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/944).

title: A35. Bootstrapping exponentially efficient WE
subfield: Witness encryption and condition-based cryptography
open: Can a witness encryption scheme that is only nontrivially exponentially efficient — say, encrypting in time far below the trivial exhaustive search — be generically amplified into full polynomial-time witness encryption, perhaps under ordinary auxiliary assumptions? In other words, is there an XWE-to-WE amplification theorem analogous to the XiO amplification known for obfuscation?
status: The best-known construction, from subexponential LWE, gives encryption time roughly \(2^{m/2}\) for \(m\)-bit witnesses (Brakerski–Jain–Komargodski–Passelègue–Wichs, 2017/2018, [*Non-Trivial Witness Encryption and Null-iO from Standard Assumptions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/874)); no general XWE-to-WE analogue of XiO amplification is known to follow from this or related techniques.
solved_when: A general construction is exhibited that takes any nontrivially exponentially efficient witness encryption scheme and, under standard auxiliary assumptions, produces polynomial-time witness encryption; no such generic amplification currently follows from existing techniques.
why: It would convert a modest exponential efficiency improvement into a foundational cryptographic primitive, upgrading weak witness encryption into a full-fledged construction from ordinary assumptions.
key_works: Brakerski–Jain–Komargodski–Passelègue–Wichs (2017/2018), [*Non-Trivial Witness Encryption and Null-iO from Standard Assumptions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/874).

title: A37. Standard-model WE for Schnorr-signature conditions
subfield: Witness encryption and condition-based cryptography
open: Can we build a condition-encryption scheme for a fixed Schnorr signature and hash instantiation, with efficiency, a standard-model security reduction, and adaptive security holding before the required signature is issued?
status: The specific target has been proposed; algebraic special-purpose witness encryption and composable gadgets exist, but ordinary witness encryption for false instances does not by itself protect true signature-existence statements. Key work: Garg–Hajiabadi–Kolonelos–Kothapalli–Policharla (2025), [A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364).
solved_when: An explicit construction is given for a fixed Schnorr signature and hash instantiation that is efficient, admits a standard-model reduction, and remains adaptively secure prior to issuance of the target signature.
why: It would tie timed release to a widely deployed, familiar signature ecosystem while giving a precisely stated security guarantee.
key_works: Garg–Hajiabadi–Kolonelos–Kothapalli–Policharla (2025), [*A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364).

title: A38. Succinct batch WE for general monotone circuit policies
subfield: Witness encryption and condition-based cryptography
open: Can one build, from plain witness encryption and standard cryptographic auxiliaries, a scheme that encrypts to an arbitrary monotone policy circuit over \(K\) NP instances while keeping the payload, per-instance cost, and overhead essentially minimal — payload polynomial in the security parameter alone, complexity comparable to encrypting to a single instance, and overhead logarithmic in \(K\)?
status: For CNF and DNF policies, succinct batch witness encryption follows from weaker tools; broader classes of bounded-space policies are achievable using iO. In existing constructions the public description of the policy circuit remains external to the ciphertext.
solved_when: *(see above)*
why: It would compress complex access conditions that combine many independent pieces of evidence into a single short ciphertext, replacing the current reliance on indistinguishability obfuscation for anything beyond CNF/DNF policies.
key_works: Devadas–Jain–Waters–Wu (2025), [*Succinct Witness Encryption for Batch Languages and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/944).

title: A40. Witness PRFs from plain witness encryption
subfield: Witness encryption and condition-based cryptography
open: Construct general NP witness PRFs from plain WE plus OWFs or LWE in the standard model, or prove a precise separation.
status: Witness PRFs imply WE and support additional applications; the reverse implication is not established by the original theory or recent WE constructions.
why: Would turn condition-based encryption into reusable condition-based pseudorandomness.
key_works: Zhandry (2014/2016), [*How to Avoid Obfuscation Using Witness PRFs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/301).

title: A44. Adaptive NP SNARGs from polynomial-security iO
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Derive adaptively sound NP SNARGs from polynomially secure iO and OWFs, eliminating subexponential hardness from the implication.
status: Waters–Wu’s 2025 theorem establishes the implication using subexponentially secure iO and OWFs without an extra algebraic assumption.
why: Would reduce the hardness needed for broadly adaptive succinct verification.
key_works: Waters–Wu (2024/2025), [*A Pure Indistinguishability Obfuscation Approach to Adaptively-Sound SNARGs for NP*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/933).

title: A48. Function-statistically-binding commitments from LWE
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Can succinct function vector commitments with function-statistical binding — the binding property needed by shadow PCPs — be constructed from ordinary LWE or comparably conventional assumptions?
status: Guan–Yogev's 2026 revision instantiates Micali's SNARG assuming LWE plus these commitments, and identifies weaker-assumption commitments as a remaining target ([Guan–Yogev 2025/2026, *Micali's SNARG, Function Vector Commitments, and Fiat–Shamir*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2328)).
solved_when: A construction of succinct function vector commitments satisfying function statistical binding is given, with security based on ordinary LWE or a similarly conventional assumption (no specialized assumption).
why: It would remove a specialized assumption from a central route to succinct arguments, namely the Micali-SNARG route via shadow PCPs.
key_works: Guan–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Micali’s SNARG, Function Vector Commitments, and Fiat–Shamir*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2328).

title: A50. Amplifying mild succinctness without knowledge extraction
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Can a mildly succinct, ordinarily sound noninteractive argument be generically amplified into a fully succinct SNARG, without assuming knowledge soundness anywhere in the construction? That is, can succinctness amplification be bootstrapped from soundness alone rather than from a witness-extraction premise?
status: The 2025 "Boosting SNARKs" theorem of Cheng–Goyal (2025) ([*Boosting SNARKs and Rate-1 Barrier in Arguments of Knowledge*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.56)) uses a SNARK — i.e., a knowledge-sound object — as its starting point, so amplification from ordinary soundness remains a separate, open target.
solved_when: A generic transformation (compiler) is given that takes any mildly succinct, ordinarily sound noninteractive argument and produces a fully succinct SNARG, with knowledge soundness never assumed of the starting object or any ingredient.
why: It would establish that compact verification can be amplified using soundness alone, removing the knowledge-extraction premise currently needed by boosting theorems.
key_works: Cheng–Goyal (2025), [*Boosting SNARKs and Rate-1 Barrier in Arguments of Knowledge*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.56).

title: A52. The unrestricted one-group-element SNARG boundary
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Is one group element really the barrier for succinct arguments in the group (generic-group) model — can we prove a lower bound for arbitrary verifiers, or is there a SNARG whose proofs are a single group element that slips past all known exclusions?
status: Existing lower bounds, notably those of Barta–Ishai–Ostrovsky–Wu (2020), [*On Succinct Arguments and Witness Encryption from Groups*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1319), hold in the Maurer generic-group model plus random oracle model under one-way functions, but only under natural restrictions on the verifier; they are not fully unrestricted impossibility theorems. Recent work (Arnon–Dujmovic–Yogev, 2025/2026, [*Pairing-Based SNARGs with Two Group Elements*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2160)) constructs SNARGs with two group elements, leaving the one-element boundary open.
solved_when: Either an unrestricted impossibility theorem rules out one-group-element SNARGs for a broad verifier class (removing the natural verifier restrictions), or an explicit construction of a SNARG with one-group-element proofs outside the currently excluded classes is given.
why: It would pin down the true minimum size of algebraic succinct proofs, settling whether the two-element constructions of Arnon–Dujmovic–Yogev are optimal.
key_works: Arnon–Dujmovic–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Pairing-Based SNARGs with Two Group Elements*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2160); Barta–Ishai–Ostrovsky–Wu (2020), [*On Succinct Arguments and Witness Encryption from Groups*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1319).

title: E02. Negligible-error two-source extraction at polylogarithmic entropy
subfield: Randomness extractors for structured sources
open: Can one explicitly construct a two-source extractor that works when each source has only polylogarithmic min-entropy in its length, and whose error is negligible — ideally of the form \(2^{-k^c}\) for some constant \(c>0\) rather than merely inverse-polynomial?
status: Recent advances achieve low-entropy two-source extraction with constant error, but these do not give negligible error; known low-error constructions require substantially more entropy.
solved_when: An explicit two-source extractor is given with \(k=\operatorname{polylog}(n)\) entropy and error \(n^{-\omega(1)}\) (ideally \(2^{-k^c}\) for a constant \(c>0\)).
why: Cryptographic applications typically require negligible error; constant or inverse-polynomial error, which current low-entropy constructions achieve, is insufficient for these uses.
key_works: Chattopadhyay–Zuckerman (2016/2019), [*Explicit Two-Source Extractors and Resilient Functions*](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2019/189-3/p01); Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33).

title: E04. Bit-fixing extraction at the sharp low-entropy boundary
subfield: Randomness extractors for structured sources
open: Can we construct explicit oblivious bit-fixing extractors that work at exactly the sharp low-entropy boundary, removing the remaining polylogarithmic overhead in the entropy requirement while still achieving long output and low error in feasible parameter regimes?
status: Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33), achieve almost-logarithmic entropy with long output and low error, leaving only a polylogarithmic overhead at the low-entropy boundary.
solved_when: An explicit bit-fixing extractor is given whose entropy requirement matches the information-theoretic boundary up to at most a constant factor, with long output length and low error in the regimes considered feasible, improving on the almost-logarithmic entropy achieved by Doron–Fridman (2025).
why: Bit-fixing sources model randomness corrupted by unknown deterministic coordinates, so sharp extractors directly yield better erasure-resilient codes, resilient functions, and protocols relying on unknown-coordinate entropy.
key_works: Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33).

title: E05. Explicit low-degree sumset extractors near random-polynomial bounds
subfield: Randomness extractors for structured sources
open: Can we explicitly and deterministically construct low-degree polynomials that extract from sumset sources with the same entropy and error trade-offs that random low-degree polynomials are known to achieve?
status: The 2025 random-polynomial framework of Alrabiah–Goodman–Mosheiff–Ribeiro (2025), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Are Good Extractors*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.38), gives strong existence theorems; deterministic explicitness remains distinct and open.
solved_when: An explicit deterministic construction of low-degree extractors for sumset sources is given, matching the entropy and error regimes achieved by the 2025 random-polynomial existence framework.
why: It would convert algebraic existence results into usable low-complexity extractors, making the polynomial-method extractor theory practical rather than merely existential.
key_works: Alrabiah–Goodman–Mosheiff–Ribeiro (2025), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Are Good Extractors*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.38).

title: E09. Samplable-source extraction from weaker circuit hardness
subfield: Randomness extractors for structured sources
open: Can multiplicative-error extractors for samplable sources be constructed under deterministic circuit-hardness assumptions alone? More precisely, the goal is to replace the nondeterministic exponential circuit-hardness premises in current constructions with ordinary deterministic circuit lower bounds.
status: Shaltiel's 2025 analysis of multiplicative extractors for samplable distributions explains why current techniques generate pseudorandomness against nondeterministic circuits and therefore require the stronger nondeterministic premises.
solved_when: A multiplicative-error extractor for samplable distributions is built whose security rests only on deterministic circuit hardness, with no nondeterministic (or stronger) lower-bound assumption.
why: It would weaken the complexity assumptions needed to clean algorithmically generated randomness, making extraction results reachable from standard deterministic lower bounds.
key_works: Shaltiel (2025), [*Multiplicative Extractors for Samplable Distributions*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.22).

title: P01. Polylogarithmic two-server information-theoretic PIR
subfield: Information-theoretic private information retrieval
open: Can two servers holding copies of an N-bit database answer a private retrieval query with only polylogarithmic total communication, where each server individually learns nothing about which bit was requested — and can this be achieved information-theoretically, without assuming the servers share free correlated setup?
status: Dvir–Gopi achieve \(\exp(O(\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}))\) communication (2014/2016, [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692)); the gap between this and logarithmic lower bounds remains enormous.
solved_when: An explicit two-server information-theoretic PIR scheme for arbitrary N-bit databases is constructed whose total communication is polylogarithmic in N, with single-server privacy and no free correlated setup.
why: It would make very short private queries possible with no computational assumptions, yielding unconditional privacy against curious servers.
key_works: Dvir–Gopi (2014/2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692).

title: P02. Superlogarithmic unrestricted two-server PIR lower bounds
subfield: Information-theoretic private information retrieval
open: Can information-theoretic private information retrieval with two servers be made to require more than logarithmically many bits of total communication, even when answers may be arbitrarily long, protocols may be nonlinear, and servers may compute without restriction?
status: No such lower bound is known; proving stronger bounds requires imposing additional answer-size, algebraic, or probe restrictions. Key works: Dvir–Gopi (2016), *2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication* (https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692); Kolby–Roy–Sternad–Yakoubov (2025), *Information-Theoretic Random-Index PIR* (https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2025.5).
solved_when: A superlogarithmic total-communication lower bound is proved for two-server PIR in the fully unrestricted regime — long answers, nonlinear protocols, and unbounded server computation.
why: It would reveal whether the current subpolynomial upper bounds are remotely optimal.
key_works: Dvir–Gopi (2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692); Kolby–Roy–Sternad–Yakoubov (2025), [*Information-Theoretic Random-Index PIR*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2025.5).

title: P04. Sublinear-time, short-message PIR with near-linear storage
subfield: Information-theoretic private information retrieval
open: Can a two-server information-theoretic PIR scheme retrieve a short record from a database without any server learning which record was requested, while keeping both the servers' storage and the client–server communication near-linear in the database size and the servers' online work genuinely sublinear? Formally, the goal is two-server information-theoretic privacy with \(N\operatorname{polylog}N\) total storage, \(N^{1-\delta}\) online probes for some fixed \(\delta>0\), and polylogarithmic communication.
status: Henzinger–Ragavan (2026) achieve quasilinear storage and sublinear probes, but their stronger communication reduction invokes computational encryption, so the purely information-theoretic regime with polylogarithmic communication remains open.
solved_when: A two-server information-theoretic PIR scheme is exhibited with \(N\operatorname{polylog}N\) storage, \(N^{1-\delta}\) online probes for a fixed \(\delta>0\), and polylogarithmic communication — all simultaneously, with no computational assumptions.
why: Low communication by itself does not stop a server from scanning the entire database on every query, so the scheme is useless in practice without sublinear online work; achieving this with near-linear storage would make efficient private retrieval realistic.
key_works: Henzinger–Ragavan (2026), [*Two-Server Private Information Retrieval in Sublinear Time and Quasilinear Space*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2008).

title: P10. Superpolynomial lower bounds for constant-query LDCs
subfield: Information-theoretic private information retrieval
open: Must every binary locally decodable code that corrects a constant fraction of errors using a fixed constant number of queries have superpolynomial block length, or does a counterexample with polynomial block length exist?
status: General lower bounds remain far below the known superpolynomial constructions, and existing restricted results — linear codes or low-query regimes — do not settle all cases. Key works include Goldreich (2024), *Lower Bounds on the Length of Locally Decodable Codes*, in [Open Problems in Honor of Luca Trevisan](https://doi.org/10.1145/3710795.3710799), and Dvir–Gopi (2016), [2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692).
solved_when: For every fixed constant query count, a superpolynomial lower bound on block length is proved for binary LDCs correcting a constant error fraction — or, alternatively, an explicit constant-query LDC with polynomial block length is constructed.
why: The answer directly determines the asymptotic communication cost achievable by information-theoretic private information retrieval, since LDC block length governs PIR query complexity.
key_works: Goldreich (2024), *Lower Bounds on the Length of Locally Decodable Codes*, in [*Open Problems in Honor of Luca Trevisan*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3710795.3710799); Dvir–Gopi (2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692).

title: C01. Logarithmic-overhead universal randomized compression
subfield: Randomized compression and seed reuse
open: Can a universal polynomial-time randomized compressor achieve overhead of just \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\) bits, given a target description length and error \(\varepsilon\)? In other words, is logarithmic overhead compatible with efficient encoding?
status: Polynomial-time constructions achieve \(O(\log m\cdot\log(n/\varepsilon))\) overhead; logarithmic overhead is known, but only via prohibitively slow compression. Key works: Bauwens (2018), [Optimal Probabilistic Polynomial Time Compression and the Slepian-Wolf Theorem: Tighter Version and Simple Proofs](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.00750); Bauwens–Zimand (2019/2023), [Universal Almost Optimal Compression and Slepian-Wolf Coding in Probabilistic Polynomial Time](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04268).
solved_when: A polynomial-time construction is given whose overhead is \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\), improving on the current \(O(\log m\cdot\log(n/\varepsilon))\).
why: It would bring universal randomized compression to information-theoretic optimality without sacrificing efficient encoding, removing the extra \(\log m\) factor that currently separates efficient constructions from the optimal ones.
key_works: Bauwens (2018), [*Optimal Probabilistic Polynomial Time Compression and the Slepian-Wolf Theorem: Tighter Version and Simple Proofs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.00750); Bauwens–Zimand (2019/2023), [*Universal Almost Optimal Compression and Slepian-Wolf Coding in Probabilistic Polynomial Time*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04268).

title: G01. Ta-Shma’s polynomial quantum-error blowup conjecture
subfield: Quantum-proof extraction and independent-process randomness
open: Does every classical strong extractor remain effective when the adversary holds quantum side information, with only a polynomial penalty in the error? Specifically, is such an extractor with m output bits and error ε always quantum-proof with error O(m√ε), granting the stipulated logarithmic extra entropy — or is there a counterexample?
status: The problem has been studied since the 2000s. Known general lifting bounds for making classical extractors quantum-proof suffer from exponential dependence on the output length, far from the conjectured polynomial O(m√ε) blowup. Key works include Berta–Fawzi–Scholz (2017), [*Quantum-proof randomness extractors via operator space theory*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2016.2627531), [arXiv:1409.3563](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3563).
solved_when: A proof that every classical strong extractor with m output bits and error ε is quantum-proof with error O(m√ε) (with the stipulated logarithmic extra entropy), or an explicit counterexample showing this bound fails.
why: A positive answer would let broad classes of classical extractors be safely reused against quantum side information, avoiding the need to design dedicated quantum-proof constructions.
key_works: Berta–Fawzi–Scholz (2017), [*Quantum-proof randomness extractors via operator space theory*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2016.2627531), [arXiv:1409.3563](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3563).

title: G04. Extraction with approximately Markov quantum side information
subfield: Quantum-proof extraction and independent-process randomness
open: If a tripartite state is only approximately Markov, in the sense that the conditional mutual information \(I(X:Y\mid E)\le\delta\), is exact-Markov-secure randomness extraction still possible with an additional error that depends only on \(\delta\) and vanishes as \(\delta\to0\) — or does there exist a counterexample where any dimension-independent bound must fail?
status: The question was explicitly raised in 2016. It is known that approximate recoverability does not automatically reproduce the exact conditional-independence structure needed for the exact-Markov security proof, so the problem remains open. The originating work is Arnon-Friedman–Portmann–Scholz (2016), [*Quantum-proof multi-source randomness extractors in the Markov model*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.TQC.2016.2), [arXiv:1510.06743](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.06743).
solved_when: Either a proof that extraction secure in the exact Markov model remains secure up to an additive error \(f(\delta)\to0\) independent of the dimensions of \(X\), \(Y\), and \(E\), or an explicit counterexample family for which no such dimension-independent bound exists.
why: Physical randomness sources essentially never satisfy exact conditional-independence assumptions, so extraction theorems restricted to exact Markov structure have limited applicability to realistic device-independent and multi-source scenarios.
key_works: Arnon-Friedman–Portmann–Scholz (2016), [*Quantum-proof multi-source randomness extractors in the Markov model*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.TQC.2016.2), [arXiv:1510.06743](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.06743).

title: G09. Quantum nonmalleable extraction with optimal seed and entropy
subfield: Quantum-proof extraction and independent-process randomness
open: Can we build a nonmalleable extractor that is optimal in both seed length and entropy requirement even when the source leaks quantum side information and the adversary may tamper with the seed? Concretely, the target is seed length \(d=O(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), min-entropy \(k=O(\log\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), and output length \(\Omega(k)\).
status: Classical constructions already reach this target; known quantum-secure constructions, such as those of Boddu–Jain–Kapshikar (2021/2024) in [*Quantum secure non-malleable-extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03097) and Li (2023) in [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802), still require polylogarithmic seed and entropy.
solved_when: An explicit construction is proved nonmalleable against quantum side information and admissible seed tampering with \(d=O(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), \(k=O(\log\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), and output \(\Omega(k)\).
why: It would make active quantum privacy amplification nearly entropy optimal, matching the classical setting's resource requirements.
key_works: Boddu–Jain–Kapshikar (2021/2024), [*Quantum secure non-malleable-extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03097); Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802).

title: G10. Two-round quantum privacy amplification with optimal loss
subfield: Quantum-proof extraction and independent-process randomness
open: Can a quantum-proof privacy amplification protocol withstand an active adversary in just two rounds while keeping nearly all of the secret entropy? Formally, starting from a weak secret with \(H_{\min}(X\mid E)\ge k\), construct an efficient two-round active protocol outputting \(k-O(\log\log n+s)\) bits with error \(2^{-s}\), valid for \(s\le ck\).
status: Two-round privacy amplification against quantum adversaries is feasible, but the known checked constructions retain roughly half of the entropy; classical protocols already achieve the stronger \(k-O(\log\log n+s)\) target. Key works: Boddu–Jain–Kapshikar (2021/2024), [*Quantum secure non-malleable-extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03097); Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802).
solved_when: An explicit, efficient two-round quantum-secure privacy amplification protocol is given that extracts \(k-O(\log\log n+s)\) bits from any source with \(H_{\min}(X\mid E)\ge k\), achieving security error \(2^{-s}\) against an active adversary for all \(s\le ck\).
why: It would preserve scarce quantum-secure entropy under an actively attacked communication channel, instead of discarding roughly half of it as current checked constructions do.
key_works: Boddu–Jain–Kapshikar (2021/2024), [*Quantum secure non-malleable-extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03097); Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802).

title: G11. Explicit seeded condensers with coefficient one on log error
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Can we explicitly construct a seeded lossless condenser whose seed length and output length match the information-theoretic optimum, with error dependence coefficient exactly one on the \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) term? Formally, achieve \(d=\log(n-k)+\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)\) and \(m=k+d+\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)\).
status: Random functions achieve the optimal leading error dependence, but general explicit constructions remain weaker. See Goodman–Li–Zuckerman (2024), [Improved Condensers for Chor-Goldreich Sources](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08142).
solved_when: An explicit seeded lossless condenser is given whose parameters match the existential bounds \(d=\log(n-k)+\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)\) and \(m=k+d+\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)\) — in particular, with leading coefficient one on the \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) error terms in both seed length and output length.
why: The coefficient of \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) controls several downstream seedless-condensing constructions, so matching it explicitly directly tightens those constructions.
key_works: Goodman–Li–Zuckerman (2024), [*Improved Condensers for Chor-Goldreich Sources*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08142).

title: G12. Constant-factor gap loss for low-entropy Chor–Goldreich sources
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Can Chor–Goldreich sources with n-bit blocks of only \(n^{0.99}\) conditional min-entropy each be condensed without losing more than a constant factor in the deficiency? Formally, the goal is rate at least 0.9 with deficiency \(O(n - n^{0.99} + \log(1/\varepsilon))\).
status: Explicit low-entropy condensation is known (Goodman–Li–Zuckerman 2024, [*Improved Condensers for Chor-Goldreich Sources*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08142)), but current constructions can enlarge the inherited deficiency by a polynomial factor rather than a constant factor.
solved_when: An explicit construction condenses n-bit blocks with at least \(n^{0.99}\) conditional min-entropy each to rate at least 0.9 while keeping the deficiency within \(O(n - n^{0.99} + \log(1/\varepsilon))\), i.e., only a constant factor larger than the inherited deficiency.
why: Without a constant-factor guarantee, repeatedly processing weak sources amplifies the deficiency polynomially and wastes most of the usable entropy; a solution would let that entropy be preserved across successive operations.
key_works: Goodman–Li–Zuckerman (2024), [*Improved Condensers for Chor-Goldreich Sources*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08142).

title: G13. Linear entropy deficiency for unpredictable sources
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Can an online adversary watching a stream of blocks condense a \((\delta,\rho)\)-unpredictable source to nearly full entropy — that is, achieve rate \(1-O(\rho)\) — rather than the weaker rate currently known? Formally, the goal is an online condenser with \(\Omega(\delta d t)\) output entropy and error polynomial in \(\rho\).
status: Doron–Moshkovitz–Oh–Zuckerman (2025), [*Online Condensing of Unpredictable Sources via Random Walks*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.30), explicitly conjecture this improvement; their random-walk construction achieves rate \(1-\rho^{1/C}\).
solved_when: An explicit online condenser for \((\delta,\rho)\)-unpredictable sources achieves rate \(1-O(\rho)\), outputs \(\Omega(\delta dt)\) bits of entropy, and incurs error polynomial in \(\rho\).
why: A solution would sharply improve the quality of randomness extracted from sources whose blocks are only occasionally predictable, which is exactly the regime left weak by current constructions.
key_works: Doron–Moshkovitz–Oh–Zuckerman (2025), [*Online Condensing of Unpredictable Sources via Random Walks*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.30).

title: G15. The online bit-fixing non-condensing conjecture
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Can a deterministic condenser nontrivially raise the entropy rate of online nonoblivious bit-fixing sources when the source has constant entropy rate, even allowing small smoothing error, or is condensation fundamentally impossible here?
